publish.title: Urgent or important? The Eisenhower matrix
publish.description: Four quadrants for deciding what to do, schedule, delegate or drop.

scenes.headline: Urgent or important?
scenes.narration: Busy is not the same as productive. Sorting your tasks takes one minute.

scenes.headline: They are not the same thing
scenes.narration: Urgent tasks demand attention now. Important tasks move you toward your goals. The Eisenhower matrix separates the two.

scenes.headline: Four quadrants
scenes.narration: Do urgent and important tasks now. Schedule important ones that are not urgent. Delegate urgent ones that are not important. Drop the rest.
items: Urgent and important: do it now

scenes.headline: Progress lives in quadrant two
scenes.narration: Important work that is not urgent, like planning and learning, is easy to postpone. Schedule it first.

scenes.headline: Where the name comes from
scenes.narration: The method is named after Dwight D. Eisenhower, who said he had two kinds of problems: the urgent and the important.

scenes.headline: Sort today's list
scenes.narration: Take today's list and mark each task with a quadrant.
